===== chart.py
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "Stage": [
        "Birth", "Age 5", "Age 15", "Age 30", "Age 50", "Age 70", "Life Expectancy"
    ],
    "Sub-Saharan Africa": [100, 82, 75, 68, 55, 35, 25],
    "South Asia": [100, 90, 83, 78, 68, 50, 38],
    "East Asia & Pacific": [100, 95, 90, 85, 78, 65, 52],
    "Latin America & Caribbean": [100, 96, 92, 88, 82, 70, 60],
    "Middle East & North Africa": [100, 94, 89, 84, 76, 62, 47],
    "Europe & Central Asia": [100, 98, 96, 93, 88, 75, 58],
    "North America": [100, 99, 98, 96, 92, 82, 70],
    "High Income Asia Pacific": [100, 99, 97, 95, 91, 80, 68]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
regions = df.columns[1:]

fig = go.Figure()

colors = [
    "#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c", "#d62728",
    "#9467bd", "#8c564b", "#e377c2", "#7f7f7f"
]

for i, region in enumerate(regions):
    fig.add_trace(go.Funnel(
        name=region,
        y=df["Stage"],
        x=df[region],
        textinfo="value+percent initial",
        marker=dict(color=colors[i]),
        hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x}<extra>%{text}</extra>"
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    title="Survival Funnel by Region: From Birth to Life Expectancy",
    funnelmode="stack",
    width=900,
    height=700,
    legend=dict(
        orientation="h",
        yanchor="bottom",
        y=1.02,
        xanchor="right",
        x=1
    ),
    margin=dict(l=50, r=50, t=80, b=50),
    plot_bgcolor="white"
)

fig.write_image("output.png")

===== summary.txt
The chart presented is a stacked funnel chart titled "Survival Funnel by Region: From Birth to Life Expectancy," which visually compares the survival rates across different age stages for various global regions. The chart is structured vertically, with the widest sections at the top, representing the starting point of 100% survival at birth, and progressively narrowing toward the bottom, reflecting declining survival rates as age increases.

Each region is represented by a distinct color: Sub-Saharan Africa in blue, South Asia in orange, East Asia & Pacific in green, Latin America & Caribbean in red, Middle East & North Africa in purple, Europe & Central Asia in brown, North America in pink, and High Income Asia Pacific in gray. The vertical axis lists the life stages from "Birth" at the top to "Life Expectancy" at the bottom, with intermediate stages at ages 5, 15, 30, 50, and 70.

At birth, all regions begin at 100%. By age 5, Sub-Saharan Africa shows a survival rate of 82%, while North America and High Income Asia Pacific both maintain a high rate of 99%. South Asia and East Asia & Pacific follow with 90% and 95%, respectively. The Middle East & North Africa and Latin America & Caribbean regions show 94% and 96%, while Europe & Central Asia stands at 98%.

By age 15, survival rates continue to decline, with Sub-Saharan Africa at 75%, South Asia at 83%, and East Asia & Pacific at 90%. Latin America & Caribbean and the Middle East & North Africa regions record 92% and 89%, respectively. Europe & Central Asia drops slightly to 96%, while North America and High Income Asia Pacific remain high at 98% and 97%.

At age 30, the rates further decrease: Sub-Saharan Africa at 68%, South Asia at 78%, and East Asia & Pacific at 85%. Latin America & Caribbean and the Middle East & North Africa show 88% and 84%, while Europe & Central Asia remains relatively high at 93%. North America and High Income Asia Pacific show 96% and 95%.

By age 50, Sub-Saharan Africa’s survival rate falls to 55%, with South Asia at 68% and East Asia & Pacific at 78%. Latin America & Caribbean and the Middle East & North Africa report 82% and 76%, respectively. Europe & Central Asia stands at 88%, while North America and High Income Asia Pacific are at 92% and 91%.

At age 70, the chart shows Sub-Saharan Africa at 35%, South Asia at 50%, and East Asia & Pacific at 65%. Latin America & Caribbean and the Middle East & North Africa record 70% and 62%, while Europe & Central Asia reaches 75%. North America and High Income Asia Pacific show higher rates at 82% and 80%.

Finally, at life expectancy, the survival rates are 25% for Sub-Saharan Africa, 38% for South Asia, and 52% for East Asia & Pacific. Latin America & Caribbean stands at 60%, while the Middle East & North Africa is at 47%. Europe & Central Asia records 58%, and North America and High Income Asia Pacific show 70% and 68%, respectively. This funnel chart effectively illustrates the progressive decline in survival rates with age across different regions, highlighting disparities in life expectancy.
